# Console report — V0.8

## What the supplied messages mean

| Console message                                | Finding                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| [vite] connecting / connected                  | Normal development-server connection messages            |
| Download React DevTools                        | Informational development hint, not an application error |
| Blocked aria-hidden … button.phone-search      | Application modal focus issue addressed in V0.3          |
| VM906 … reportAllChanges … undefined.startTime | Origin not established; not claimed fixed                |

## Focus fix

The old search overlay used a controlled Radix dialog without its own trigger, together with custom requestAnimationFrame focus restoration. Background hiding could run while the triggering phone-search button still held focus, and focus could be restored before the overlay finished closing.

The shared Modal now uses the native HTML dialog element and showModal/close. The browser coordinates modality, background inertness, initial focus, Escape cancellation and opener restoration. Search, resource details, collection dialogs, study editing, mobile navigation and appearance all use this lifecycle. No global console filtering, aria-hidden removal loop, or accessibility-disable workaround is installed.

The route focus effect also checks whether focus moved after navigation started; it no longer overrides a newly opened menu/dialog.

Relevant primary documentation:

- [WAI: native HTML dialog technique](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H102)
- [WAI modal dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)
- [HTML dialog specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element)

### Verify in your browser

1. Keep the Console visible and use the phone navigation search button.
2. Confirm the search input receives focus, Tab stays inside the modal, and background links cannot receive focus.
3. Press Escape. Focus should return to the opening search button.
4. Search for cardiac, open The cardiac cycle, then close details. Confirm a single modal is open at a time.
5. Repeat with the mobile menu, appearance switcher, collection editor and calendar editor.
6. Navigate between public and personal pages; verify route focus and no repeated aria-hidden warnings.

DOM tests exercise our open/close lifecycle with a native-dialog test double. They do not prove the real browser's top-layer or assistive-technology behavior.

## The `VM###` / `startTime` exception

`VM272`, `VM906` and similar names are runtime-generated script labels, not stable source filenames. The earlier supplied stack contains `reportAllChanges` inside an anonymous two-line script. That symbol is absent from the MedClub source and from the inspected React, React DOM, Framer Motion, Radix, cmdk, Vite and TanStack runtime package trees. This is therefore not a MedClub component exception. It is injected by the preview host, developer tooling or a browser extension.

Do not add global error suppression or random `startTime` checks to MedClub components. There is no corresponding failing statement in the supplied source to patch, and hiding it would also hide real failures.

Practical resolution:

1. Open the same localhost page in an Incognito/InPrivate window with extensions disabled.
2. If the exception disappears, re-enable extensions one at a time and update or remove the one that injects `reportAllChanges`.
3. If it remains only inside an embedded site preview, open the Vite localhost URL directly. The preview's monitoring layer is the source.
4. If it remains in a clean direct browser session, enable **Pause on uncaught exceptions**, click the `VM###:2` source link and inspect its source URL. A `chrome-extension://` URL identifies the extension; a preview-host URL identifies the host.
5. The two Vite connection messages and the React DevTools suggestion are informational, not errors.

If it remains in a clean direct session, inspect the integrating project's `index.html` and Vite plugins for extra monitoring code; setup files are not part of this source-only delivery. The script origin and the small function around `reportAllChanges`, with credentials or tokens removed, are the missing details required for a targeted patch.

[Chrome DevTools JavaScript debugging reference](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/javascript/reference)

This release cannot certify that an unidentified script outside the provided source has been fixed.

Required styling packages: `tailwindcss` 4, `tw-animate-css`, and either your existing Tailwind Vite integration or `@tailwindcss/postcss` 4. The verification build used TypeScript 5.9.3 and Vite 8.0.13.

For an existing React project missing these runtime dependencies:

```bash
npm install react-router-dom @tanstack/react-query framer-motion radix-ui lucide-react cmdk sonner clsx class-variance-authority tailwind-merge tw-animate-css
```

Configure Tailwind 4 once in the existing project. For a PostCSS setup, install `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/postcss` and use:

```js
// postcss.config.mjs
export default { plugins: { "@tailwindcss/postcss": {} } };
```

Do not keep a Tailwind 3 PostCSS configuration alongside this one. The stylesheet imports Tailwind itself; do not also import the Vite starter CSS. Keep TypeScript JSX mode `react-jsx`, DOM types and Vite client types enabled. No path alias is needed.

The source contains no external credentials, live API URL, downloadable course files or remote font dependency.

Manrope (Latin, variable 200–800) and Noto Sans Arabic (Arabic, variable 100–900) are included as WOFF2 files with their SIL Open Font License notices. They are served from the source assets, with `font-display: swap`. No font package or external font provider is required in your existing project.

# V0.1 visual and personal-workspace revision

The content/services architecture is retained. The application shell and visual composition are redesigned.

| Area                        | Revised behavior                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

`AppearanceProvider` owns typed navigation orientation and `sidebarCollapsed` values in the existing `medclub.appearance.v1` storage record. A future account-settings adapter can replace persistence and retain the UI contract.

V0.8 adds the browser-local account preview and editable identity. Preferences and account data are still device-local; production sessions and server-synced preferences remain future work.

## Verification

Strict TypeScript and production build pass. Exact results are recorded in `V0.1-CHECKLIST.md`.

The browser security policy blocked the local visual preview, so real-device layout and pixel-level visual acceptance remain unverified. The delivered archive contains only the updated `src/` tree; the temporary verification harness and development dependencies are excluded.

# Personal workspace extension points

The public experience and My MedClub are independent route layouts. The shared providers keep saved items, language and appearance stable while the page frame changes.

## Sidebar

`SidebarToggle` is used by both sidebars. `AppearanceProvider` stores `{ navigation, sidebarCollapsed }` under the existing `medclub.appearance.v1` key. Older orientation-only records work without a migration step; absent collapse state means expanded. Invalid storage uses the default vertical, expanded sidebar. If a write fails, the changed state still works for the session.

At widths of 768 px and above, vertical navigation can collapse to a 76 px icon rail. `NavigationHint` adds hover/focus labels in this mode; accessible link names remain in the DOM. The compact Learn disclosure opens beside the public rail. Horizontal navigation ignores the compact state visually while retaining its value. Phones always use the bottom dock.

## Personal layout and routes

`PersonalLayout` mounts its own navigation and header. The public footer and public menu are not mounted. All personal subpages share that frame; only the content changes. The header includes Back to MedClub, scoped search, language and settings. The default entry is the dashboard at `/my`; identity details are at `/my/profile`.

`SpaceTransition` detects crossings between `/my/*` and public routes. It keys only that boundary and uses a short opacity transition with a fading tint. It honors reduced motion and avoids transforming the fixed-navigation ancestor. Direct loads do not play an entrance transition. Overlays close on route changes, and the personal not-found page links back into the personal home.

`useWorkspacePaths` chooses public or personal course URLs and breadcrumb roots. Use it for new reusable academic components so a personal link does not unexpectedly open the public shell. Personal search filters results using the profile's course IDs and navigates to `/my/learning/:slug`.

## Data and persistence

`StudentProfile` is defined in `types/student.ts`. `MedClubServices.personal.getProfile()` supplies it, currently from `data/mock/student.ts`. Set its `courseIds` to existing course IDs. Its `focusMinutes` initializes the personal timer; it is not a count of time spent. Dashboard saved counts are computed from records that still exist, using the same selector as the library.

Only sample identity is shown. Browser-local saved items and preferences are working features; authentication, editable identity, account-specific storage and server synchronization are not implemented. A future signed-in implementation must provide real backend access checks and account-scoped persistence. The visual separation is not a security boundary.

No new package dependencies were added for this revision. Replace the complete `src` tree together, since routes, service types, providers, translations and shared cards changed alongside the new pages.

# MedClub V0.13.10 — Dark palette and readable controls

Replace the complete `src/` directory, retaining the existing manifest, lockfile
and project configuration. This is based on the verified 401-file V0.13.9 archive.
No dependency, model, image or external service was added.

## What changed

- The dark theme separates neutral reading surfaces from colored category surfaces.
  Coral, amber, olive, green, teal, blue, violet and rose have independent ink/fill
  pairs. 216 legacy color references were assigned appropriate accent tokens while
  retaining their exact light-mode fallback values.
- Dark red-russet navigation uses a restrained fixed gradient with white type.
  Content uses charcoal-plum surfaces; the whole page is not tinted brown or wine.
  Gradients are static CSS backgrounds with no animation loop or new media payload.
- Resource thumbnails, academic batch progress, product visuals, media cards,
  recruitment roles, calendar categories, workflow statuses, Admin metrics and
  governance role glyphs retain category color. Existing course book-cover hues
  remain. Status labels continue to carry meaning alongside their colors.
- Quiet gradients give the Community, academic, mentorship, contribution, event
  and opportunity surfaces depth. Event/opportunity card transforms were not changed.
- Corrected selected Store navigation, dark notebook return links/import glyphs,
  category-colored metric icons, dim course-cover descriptions, inputs, placeholders,
  native select options and browser autofill text. Selected backgrounds no longer
  reuse a light foreground token.
- Desktop header height is 64px instead of 76px; the phone minimum is 60px instead
  of 68px. Existing action dimensions, search anchoring, fixed sidebar, hover tools,
  fittings and 200px-down/50px-up scroll thresholds remain.
- Existing Light/Dark/System settings, Arabic RTL and reduced motion remain. Source
  PDFs and other media are not inverted or recolored; the existing evening campus
  renderer still controls 3D lighting. The fallback poster retains more saturation.

## Attached console log

- Replaced `PCFSoftShadowMap` with `PCFShadowMap`. The installed Three.js renderer
  explicitly reports that the former was removed and already falls back to the
  latter. This removes the application's deprecated-shadow warning without
  changing its effective shadow technique.
- Language, theme and Honors controls now use non-modal menus. The installed menu
  library's modal path calls `hideOthers`, which can hide the surrounding workspace
  while route focus moves. These navigation menus retain arrow-key selection,
  Escape and outside dismissal without hiding the page. Actual dialogs remain modal.
- The supplied Similarweb CORS/fetch messages originate from its browser extension.
  No unrelated endpoint or browser security policy was modified.
- Development-time long-task/reflow notices alone do not establish production frame

A cover opens once, a compact toolbar replaces campus distractions, and Back to courses uses the current workspace.   worker, fonts, CMaps and image-decoding assets. No manifest or lockfile change

  load only when opening a PDF; there are no CDN requests.
- Pages are rendered as needed, with nearby-page prefetching, at most two raster
  jobs and eight cached page rasters per document. Raster density is capped for
  phones. This bounds the page cache, not total memory for every possible PDF.
- The fold is an interactive CSS 3D paper effect with real page surfaces, not a

  the original file remains the reference for such documents.

# MedClub V0.13.13 — A quieter study desk and private student tools

Replace the entire `src/` folder. Retain your existing React, TypeScript, Vite,
Tailwind configuration and dependencies. This source-only release starts from
exact V0.13.12 and preserves the earlier routes, workspaces, governance, import
permissions, PDF reader, themes, navigation, transitions and resource workflows.
No dependency or backend is added. Connected Learning Materials remains excluded.

## Study space

- The notebook occupies the available screen, with a non-sticky compact course
  toolbar. The document does not scroll at the tested study viewport sizes.
  Reading, zoomed PDFs, long file lists and open tool panels can scroll internally.
- Wider readers retain the real two-page PDF spread and centre binding. Narrower
  readers and phones use one page. PDF paper and document colours stay intact.
- The section rail has static subject icons, expands on hover or keyboard focus,
  and supports a touch interaction. Its close control leaves a thin usable rail.
  There is no expand/collapse button. Bookmarks keep their vertical click positions
  when the rail changes width. Section previews attach to the matching bookmark;
  low-positioned previews are bounded by the screen and retain their connecting edge.
- In explicit Study focus, campus navigation is hidden and inert and has no
  reveal button, edge hint or hover trigger. Exit study focus or Back to courses
  restores the normal workspace controls. Upward reading scroll never reveals
  campus navigation. Normal campus folding and scrolling behaviour stays intact.
- A small movable timer/notes/GPA strip uses pointer capture on its grip. Drag with
  mouse or touch, or focus the grip and use arrows (Shift for larger steps).
  Home, double-clicking the grip, or Reset position returns it to the lower centre.
  Its drawer stays attached to it. Position is bounded and restored per study key.
- Section reading positions are internal notebook positions rather than document
  scroll positions. File selection and individual PDF pages still restore independently.
- Interactive paper surfaces now have a bent outer strip, front/back content and
  crease lighting. The paper is clipped to the notebook's reading frame. Half-turns
  show actual upcoming PDF pages; file/section boundary previews use the target's
  remembered page, or real section resources when no file is selected. A limited
  low-resolution preview cache prepares a target at a boundary. Loading and unavailable
  files remain explicit. Overview previews use actual course text and outcomes.
- The fold remains a CSS 3D effect, not a Blender model or physical paper simulation.
  Mouse/touch gestures, short-drag return, explicit Previous/Next, arrow keys,
  Arabic direction and reduced-motion alternatives remain available.

## Student notes and GPA

Notes are available only to signed-in users. Both types are private:

| Type | Association |
| --- | --- |
| General | No course; useful for planning or personal study notes |
| Course | Course picker; attached to the chosen course and still private |

Create and choose multiple notes, give them titles, write and save, insert a current
PDF page reference, download a plain-text copy or confirm deletion. Notes autosave
and are isolated by account in device-local storage. Course attachments do not
publish them. Old signed-in course scratch notes migrate once and remain recoverable
without reappearing after deletion. Storage errors retain the draft and offer download.
Notes waiting for a course are not silently converted into general notes.

The GPA calculator accepts actual credits and numeric grade points on an editable
maximum-point scale. It weights points by credits, permits valid zero grades,
optionally combines earlier cumulative credits/GPA, and explicitly excludes
pass/fail or withdrawn rows. Empty and invalid calculations do not show plausible
scores. No institution-specific percentage-to-grade conversion is assumed; the
previous supplied text did not contain a recoverable grading policy. It is a
planning estimate, not an official transcript. Signed-in inputs persist privately
on this device; guests may try the calculator without saved account inputs.

Notes and GPA also appear in the existing `/my/focus` and `/utilities` tools area.
The original focus timer and checklist remain included.

## Section and batch artwork

Seven generated static scenes appear in Learning, Community, Mentorship, Join the
team, Get involved and Store, plus the academic batch gate. Events, Opportunities
and Contributions share the Get involved scene because they belong to that main
section. The supplied Home image remains the default. Gate cards retain working
links, batch colours, year, term and progress data, with a small optional image zoom.

The assets are 640px and 1280px WebPs in `assets/section-art/`, about 1.29 MB combined.
Only the displayed image variant is fetched. The asset manifest records the built-in
image-generation method, scene prompt summaries and filenames. No generated image
contains UI text; headings and controls remain live, localized HTML.

Users with existing `content.publish` or `builder.manage` capabilities can use
Edit image directly on a page hero or on the batch page. They can choose a validated
PNG/JPEG/WebP, supply English and Arabic descriptions, save a compressed image and
restore the original. Writes check authentication and capability inside the local
service, including a second check after image processing. Images reject unsupported
formats, MIME spoofing, oversize input and unavailable storage. The optional typed
`ArtworkService` is a replacement boundary for a future shared CMS adapter.

These hero edits remain device-local in the current preview. They do not deploy,
sync to visitors' devices or replace the existing Admin Page Builder. Production
requires a server/storage implementation with equivalent authorization. Notes and
GPA are also device-local; the ZIP does not contain user-created notes or PDFs.

  production build pass. The complete source contains 655 files: 604 original

  software-keyboard variations, sustained frame rate and a complete accessibility

# MedClub V0.13.4 — Campus prototype

This is a real mesh-based 3D prototype integrated into the exact V0.13.3 source.
It is NOT the exact supplied image rebuilt in Blender. Architecture, people,
vegetation, materials and lighting are simplified. No verified .blend file was
created because Blender could not run in the authoring environment.

## Install

Replace your complete `src/` directory with this archive's `src/` directory.
Keep your existing project configuration. Add the new dependencies:

```sh
npm install three@0.186.0
npm install --save-dev @types/three@0.183.1
```

The GLB and fallback images are inside `src/assets/campus` and are resolved
through Vite. No public-directory copy, CDN, or external 3D service is needed.
Do not discard your existing package.json or lockfile.

## What changes

- Home uses the full-width campus in its opening section, with six existing
  destinations linked from the corresponding buildings and accessible HTML links.
- Registration and verification show the same campus with shutters closed and
  people absent. Sign-in and recovery show the community campus.
- Desktop loads 3D only when the scene enters the viewport. Phones, data-saving
  connections and reduced-motion users start with the model's rendered preview
  and can explicitly open 3D.
- The active scene has restrained figure movement, pointer parallax, hover
  highlighting, left/right/center camera controls and a pause button.
- Canvas rendering stops offscreen and when the document is hidden. Pixel ratio
  is capped at 1.5, animation at 30 fps, and shadow maps are computed once.
- Failed WebGL/model loading keeps the preview and ordinary navigation usable.
- Interface labels have English and Arabic versions. Signs inside the model are
  English geometry; accessible Arabic navigation sits outside the canvas.

## Preserved baseline

Only two original production files changed: `features/homepage/sections/Hero.tsx`
and `app/layouts/AuthLayout.tsx`. All 362 other V0.13.3 files are byte-for-byte
unchanged; no original source files were deleted. The former particle-field
component remains in the source but is no longer mounted in the auth layout.

## What is not implemented

- Photorealistic reconstruction or exact matching of the reference image.
- A verified Blender project or verified execution of the supplied import script.
- Earned building upgrades, levels, per-account campus persistence or awards.
  These visuals are presentation states, not claimed measurements of activity.
- Skeletal character walking: figure movement is a restrained positional loop.
- Browser/device visual acceptance and measured real-device frame rate.

The suggested progression mapping is: learning → recorded study milestones;
media → approved publications; community → recorded participation; mentorship →
completed sessions; contribution → accepted work; journals → accepted editorial
or research work. Define and validate these events before displaying earned
upgrades. Do not reduce building quality because a student takes a break.

## Assets and verification

The model contains 19 named meshes, including all six buildings, separate
activity/shutter layers and the central stethoscope landmark. Its 67,644
triangles occupy 2,697,772 bytes as standard indexed GLB.

Khronos glTF validation: zero errors and warnings. The model also parsed with
the actual Three.js GLTFLoader used by the website. The active/dormant preview
images were rendered from its triangles using a CPU rasterizer; browser lighting
will differ. TypeScript and production build passed. Focused auth/navigation/PDF
and campus checks passed (11 tests). The complete inherited regression plus
new campus checks passed: 215/215, with no failures, skips or cancellations.
Browser visual QA and execution of the Blender script remain unverified.

The Three.js renderer remains a separately requested ~615 kB chunk (~155 kB
gzip). The existing shared entry is ~993 kB (~306 kB gzip); the bundle warning
remains. A small GLB is not proof of fast rendering on every device.

The companion 3D assets package includes the same GLB, a Blender import script,
the reproducible model generator, and both model previews.

Technical references: [Three.js](https://threejs.org/docs/) and
[Blender glTF importer/exporter](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF-Blender-IO).

# MedClub V0.13.7 — Notebook frame and adaptive color modes

Replace your complete `src/` directory. Retain your current project configuration,
package.json, lockfile and dependencies, including Three.js. No package was added.

## Navigation and search

- The default desktop sidebar is fixed, inset from the screen edge and rounded at
  the bottom. Its top joins the header through one continuous surface and a curved
  inner corner. The existing light palette and separate selected-tab pills remain.
- Two small metal binding fittings decorate each bar without receiving pointer or
  keyboard input. On phones the header fittings shrink; controls remain compact.
- The expanded logo/toggle arrangement, collapsed hover toggle, fixed positioning,
  shadow reveal, pinning and hover-only action tray from V0.13.6 remain included.
- Search records the control that opened it and positions the same search panel
  at that control, with a short origin-based reveal. A search opened from the
  bottom navigation opens upward. Placement clamps to the visible viewport and
  adjusts for resize, RTL and the mobile keyboard. Shortcuts use a visible trigger
  when available. A 5px backdrop blur softens the page behind the panel.
- Native modal focus containment, Escape, outside dismissal and focus restoration
  are retained. Closing is immediate so keyboard focus is never delayed.

## Page continuity

- A single routed page tree fades out over 140ms; the destination fades in over
  240ms. Navigation and the fixed header remain outside these content transforms.
- Visited routes restore their reading position in the current app session.
  Browser Back uses saved history-entry positions. First visits begin at the top
  while the page is faded out. Filters and notebook section changes keep their
  existing independent behavior.
- Restoration waits for lazy modules and query-driven loading states. Hash targets
  that appear later remain supported. Loading feedback stays visible.
- Outgoing page content and footer links become inert during the fade, preventing
  stale destinations from receiving a click as their layout is replaced.
- Rapid navigation discards superseded arrivals. Focus moves only when it will
  not interrupt a newer menu/dialog interaction. Reduced motion skips the delays.

## Light, Dark and System

- A dedicated selector sits beside language in public, personal, admin and auth
  headers. It persists the choice, synchronizes across tabs and defaults to the
  computer setting. Existing navigation preferences migrate without being reset.
- Dark mode uses warm charcoal surfaces, ivory reading text and softened russet
  accents. Legacy surfaces use separate ink, fill and boundary color aliases;
  each alias preserves the original light color as its fallback.
- Academic notebook paper, course accents, forms, dialogs, notifications and
  workspace surfaces have corresponding dark colors. Source PDFs and other
  original media are not inverted or recolored.
- Active and dormant 3D campuses follow the resolved theme. Dark mode selects
  evening lighting; the active campus retains warm illuminated buildings while
  registration stays dormant. The non-WebGL poster also adapts. Theme changes do
  not reload the model, and the existing motion/performance limits remain.

## Preservation and verification

All 382 V0.13.6 source files are retained. Forty-eight original files changed,
mostly to provide theme-aware color fallbacks. Eight files were added, including
these notes, for a complete 390-file source archive. Routes, permissions,
PDF workflows, saved content and all earlier features remain included.

- 242 distinct regression checks passed across the full run and focused reruns.
  The full run exposed one lost-click issue in the journal-to-library flow. After
  correcting the outgoing footer, the original community suite passed 7/7;
  all 15 affected navigation/theme checks also passed on the corrected source.
- Strict TypeScript and the final production build passed.
- Legacy light-mode color declarations were checked against V0.13.6; their
  fallbacks preserve the original values. Core dark reading/control color pairs
  meet a 4.5:1 text contrast threshold; this is not a full accessibility audit.
- Source-only archive integrity and byte comparison passed.

Real-browser visual QA remains unavailable in this environment. Automated tests
cannot establish the appearance of the binding fittings, rendered mobile/RTL

# MedClub V0.13.9 — Community overview and independent header

Replace the complete `src/` directory. Keep the existing dependencies, manifest,
lockfile and build configuration. This update adds no package, image or 3D asset.
The baseline is the exact 392-file V0.13.8 source archive.

## Community

- Shorter secondary navigation with static destination icons and persistent text
  labels. At 1150px and below, Honors groups Honor Plate and Hall of Honor in an
  accessible menu. Both original URLs remain, including Arabic navigation.
- A record-derived overview replaces the decorative signal chart: unique public
  activities, published journal articles, open team roles, and the nearest valid
  upcoming event. Each value links to the relevant content.
- The recruitment schema does not identify leadership vacancies. The UI therefore
  says **Open team roles**, not leadership opportunities. Counts are position
  records with remaining openings, not a sum of seats or applications.
- The default service still uses illustrative records. The card explicitly says
  **Preview records** and uses the service's declared **3 September 2026** sample
  calendar. These are not production statistics. A live adapter can declare its
  own snapshot date or omit it to use the current date.
- Loading and failure states do not display false zero counts. Retry reloads the
  service queries. A genuinely empty event list shows an explicit empty state.
- The hero uses a more balanced information panel and two headline groups:
  “Medicine” / “is learned together.” Narrow widths can wrap further. Controls,
  cards and panels use scoped 10/16/24px radii. Decorative rings and signal lines
  were removed while the typography, light palette and spacing character remain.

## Header, sidebar and search

- Public, personal and admin headers are independent of the fixed rounded sidebar.
  An opaque backing still masks the upper gap while the header is visible.
- Deliberate downward scrolling hides the header after 200px. An upward movement
  of 50px reveals it. Reversing direction resets accumulated distance; returning
  near the document top reveals it. Negative overscroll is clamped.
- The header folds backward around its top edge in 340ms, with a 220ms fade. The
  same transition reverses on reveal. Reduced motion skips spatial movement.
- Search, dialogs, menus, header focus/hover and route transitions keep the header
  visible. Tab reveals it. A hidden header is inert and excluded from the accessible
  tree; keyboard focus is never deliberately hidden inside it.
- Search is ready with the shell rather than waiting for the detail-overlay chunk.
  Native modality opens and explicitly focuses the input in the opening gesture.
  The existing adjacent input, anchored results, Escape, outside dismissal,
  filtering and opener-focus restoration remain. Detail overlays stay lazy-loaded.
- Appearance remains visible in the public/admin sidebar. Only pin/hide controls
  reveal on hover or keyboard focus, over the existing compact status row. Touch
  retains access to these controls. Revealing this tray no longer adds footer
  height. Decorative fittings use fixed viewport-clamped offsets instead of a
  percentage of the rail's changing height.
- Sidebar selection is quieter than the active Community section. Language glyphs,
  Appearance slider knobs and the color-mode halo have brief hover feedback on
  fine pointers, disabled by reduced-motion preferences.

## Dark details

Wine navigation remains. Teal, blue, violet, amber and rose provide small category
accents in the overview, community cards, event tickets/statuses, recruitment and
course tabs. New foreground/fill pairs meet 4.5:1 computed contrast. Light/Dark/
System, existing campus night lighting, RTL and forced-color fallbacks remain.
PDF source pages and other original media are not recolored.

- Full inherited and new regression: **262/262 passed** (251 inherited, 11 new).

  focus holds, route resets, search typing in the opening gesture, retry and empty

# MedClub V0.10 design direction

## Concept: the clinical control room

Admin is a separate operational product, not a public page with extra buttons. The V0.10 shell shifts into a dark diagnostic environment while preserving the red/russet MedClub identity. Warm content surfaces sit inside a focused control plane so long review sessions remain readable.

## Signature behavior

- A restrained ECG signal, diagnostic rings and breathing control mark establish the admin world on arrival.
- Navigation icons run a short instrument-check motion on hover; active icons emit a quiet diagnostic ring.
- Metric cards expose their signal color through a fast scan instead of generic scale animation.
- Content review uses a queue-and-inspector workbench on large screens and a stable stacked flow on smaller screens.
- Activity history pairs searchable operations with a before/after inspector.
- Version comparison places the current and selected snapshots side by side; restoration explicitly creates a new version.
- V0.8 authentication remains the only WebGL surface. Admin motion is CSS-only and operational.

## UX rules

- Nothing moves directly from review to publication. Approval and publication are separate decisions.
- Requesting changes requires an explanatory note.
- Publication requires an approved state, confirmed rights and at least one reference.
- Activity history offers no edit or delete operation.
- Restoration preserves every previous version and appends a new audit event.
- Preview access is visibly separated from production authorization.
- The admin navigation follows the existing vertical/horizontal preference on larger screens and becomes a fixed horizontal dock on phones.

## Accessibility and responsive rules

- Every workbench preserves a linear DOM order: queue first, inspector second.
- Status is always represented by text, not color alone.
- Scrollable tab and navigation regions hide native bars without disabling touch, wheel or keyboard input.
- Mobile controls remain at least 44 px and form text remains zoom-safe.
- Logical properties and mirrored directional icons support Arabic RTL.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` removes scans, pulses, orbiting and hover displacement.

## Honest boundary

V0.10 demonstrates admin operations with device-local sample data. It does not implement production permissions. V0.12 remains responsible for capability enforcement, protected founders, high-risk approval and immutable server audit storage.

# MedClub V0.11 design direction

## Concept: the living clinical canvas

The page builder extends the V0.10 control room without becoming a generic rectangular CMS. Dark instrument controls frame a warm page canvas. Red diagnostic pulses identify active state, while the actual page remains readable and close to its public appearance.

- Palette icons perform a short instrument check on hover.
- The canvas narrows smoothly between desktop, tablet and phone frames.
- Selected blocks expose a floating instrument strip with drag, move, duplicate and delete controls.
- Audience and schedule rules remain visible as annotations instead of being hidden in settings.
- Autosave behaves like a quiet cloud signal; it never blocks composition.
- Preview uses the exact structured block renderer used inside the canvas.

## UX rules

- The page is data, not hard-coded JSX or arbitrary HTML.
- Drag and drop is never the only reordering mechanism.
- Published edits return to draft until explicitly republished.
- Publishing and scheduling save the latest canvas first.
- Restoration creates a new draft revision and keeps all milestone history.
- Local image uploads are visibly described as preview-only.
- Status, audience and save state always include text, not only color.

## Responsive and accessibility rules

- Desktop uses a three-zone palette, canvas and inspector workbench.
- Medium layouts keep the canvas primary and move the inspector below it.
- Phones present canvas, block library and inspector in task order above the existing admin dock.
- Navigation and editor scrollers hide native bars while retaining touch, wheel and keyboard scrolling.

- Reduced motion removes scans, orbiting, pulses and width interpolation.

## Honest boundary

V0.11 is a complete front-end CMS preview backed by device-local structured documents. Its Publish action updates the preview repository; it does not deploy a public website. Production needs a server publishing pipeline, validated rich text, durable media storage, scheduling jobs, cache invalidation, permissions and immutable audit integration.

# V0.12.1 — Navigation and academic notebook

This is the requested UI/study refinement of V0.12. It does not advance or replace the planned V0.13 analytics milestone. The complete V0.1–V0.12 source remains included.

## Scope

- Main public navigation retreats on downward scrolling and returns on upward intent. Pages with secondary navigation also retract after entry. The personal rail uses this behavior inside course pages; Admin navigation remains unchanged.
- A labeled, illuminated edge handle supports pointer hover, keyboard focus and tap. Navigation can be pinned. Small scroll changes are ignored; navigation interactions, dialogs and menus prevent automatic dismissal. Hidden navigation is inert.
- Section pages allocate their reading space independently of transient navigation visibility. Scroll-driven reveals overlay content instead of changing its width. Horizontal, vertical, mobile and RTL navigation are supported.
- Course sections become an academic notebook with dimensional cover surfaces, a metallic binding, page-stack edges, paper bookmarks and directional 320 ms page turns. The text remains a flat, single accessible content tree. Course accents are preserved: russet, red, olive and purple.
- Bookmarks show the real count and first resource title before interaction. Hover/focus previews show section content, resource names and available metadata. Escape dismisses previews. Touch selection opens directly.
- The notebook remembers the active section, selected material, relative section scroll, reader scroll, explicit PDF page bookmark, supplied recording playback time and split-view preferences per account and course, locally on this device.
- Study focus retains the course title and section controls, reduces surrounding UI and turns off notebook animation. Escape or the visible exit control restores normal study mode. Focus does not carry into another route.
- Split view allows a manually chosen companion resource. It remains independent of the primary section, so a recording can stay beside notes. Wide layouts have an accessible width slider; narrower layouts stack the readers.
- Resource previews use supplied excerpts/thumbnails/chapters when available, otherwise the existing description. Contributor and update metadata are retained; missing reviewer/reference information is explicitly identified.
- Existing save, details, reviewed-state and preview-history actions remain integrated.

Connected learning materials were explicitly excluded. No automatic links between related lectures, slides, notes or questions were added.

## What remains unchanged

The original homepage, brand asset, auth/WebGL world, academic catalog/batch/year pages, community page content, events, opportunities, mentorship, contributions, store, recruitment, personal feature pages, Admin/CMS/governance behavior, service implementations and seed datasets remain unchanged. The seven edited original files are the public/personal layouts, provider composition, navbar wrapper, course page, optional resource type fields and stylesheet import entry. All other original source files are byte-identical to the recovered V0.12 archive.

## Try the update

- `/learn/courses/human-anatomy` has all nine sections, several existing resource types and a russet notebook.
- `/learn/courses/cardiovascular-physiology` demonstrates the red theme.
- `/learn/courses/cell-biology` demonstrates the olive theme.
- `/learn/courses/clinical-neurology` demonstrates the purple theme.
- `/my/learning/human-anatomy` uses the existing protected personal frame.
- `/community` demonstrates the main-navigation retreat with a secondary navigation bar.

## Files and playback

The supplied V0.12 seed resources have `fileUrl: null`. No educational documents, recording contents, excerpts, reviewer identities or references were fabricated. Those resources display their existing descriptions and an honest file-unavailable state.

Resource fields added as optional API data:

```ts
mediaType?: "video" | "audio" | "pdf" | "image" | "external";
preview?: {
  excerpt?: Text;
  thumbnailUrl?: string;
  chapters?: { title: Text; seconds: number }[];
};
reviewer?: Text;
references?: { title: Text; url?: string }[];
```

Provide a real `fileUrl` and preferably an explicit `mediaType` for inline reading/playback. Recognized file extensions provide a fallback; arbitrary external pages open as links instead of being embedded. Native audio/video use controls, metadata-only preload and no autoplay. Only selected material/companion viewers mount. The original-file link remains available for unsupported formats or embedding restrictions.

PDF page state uses the visible page-bookmark input. The browser's native PDF viewer does not expose internal scroll/page changes to this React app; those changes cannot be captured automatically. PDF support depends on the browser; use the original-file link where necessary. Live playback/network performance still depends on the supplied media host and files.

## Persistence and performance

- `medclub:study:v1:<encoded-account>:<encoded-course>` stores study preferences and positions. Guest positions have their own key. It is a device-local convenience, not a backend record or authorization layer.
- Position events update refs rather than rerendering the notebook on every scroll/time tick. Writes are debounced; visibility/page-hide/unmount flush remaining positions. Corrupt or invalid stored values are normalized safely. Storage failures preserve the currently mounted session state and show a session-only notice.
- `medclub:navigation:pinned:v1` stores the device's navigation pin preference. Existing workspace/auth/storage keys are unchanged.
- No new packages, models, raster textures, WebGL canvas or animation-frame loop were added. The notebook uses CSS 3D transforms on functional page layers; this is not a Blender asset.
- Notebook JS and CSS are loaded with the existing lazy CoursePage route. Navigation scroll listeners use a single pending frame and passive events. Reduced-motion and forced-colors variants are included.
- The inherited shared main-bundle size warning remains. Build configuration is deliberately unchanged in this source-only delivery.

## Integration and validation

Replace the entire existing `src/` with this archive's `src/`. Keep the existing package setup. No additional dependencies are required.

Validation completed: **179/179 regression tests passed**, strict TypeScript passed, and the production build passed. The final 11-test study/navigation suite also passed after the last focus-management adjustment. The preserved V0.12 verification setup was used. The inherited regression suite and the added study/navigation behavior suite cover selection, persistence, account/course separation, previews, focus mode, split view, navigation reveal/pinning, RTL state and supplied-media resume handling.

DOM tests do not verify real browser layout, native PDF integration, rendering smoothness or device frame rate. Final device acceptance should cover 320/390 px mobile, tablet, wide desktop, Arabic, increased text size, touch, keyboard focus, reduced motion, long resource lists and real source files. No real-browser visual QA was performed in this delivery.

# MedClub V0.13.15 — Study refinements

Replace the existing `src/` directory with this complete tree. It retains all V0.1–V0.13.14 modules, routes, assets, theme tokens and access rules; no new runtime dependency is required.

## Reading and study tools

- PDF pages fit the available reading width instead of shrinking to the available height. Two pages remain on wide screens, one on phones and companion readers. Zoom and native document scrolling remain available outside Study focus.
- The compact labelled tool strip moves by dragging its half-width upper grip. Only the grip captures pointer gestures. Arrow keys move it, Shift increases the step, and Home or double-click restores its default position. Position is saved per account and course and clamped when the viewport changes. Pointer updates use one animation frame; the drawer follows the strip and stays on screen.
- A started or paused timer remains visible above its icon after closing the drawer. Near the top of the viewport it appears below the icon. The absolute-time countdown recomputes on visibility changes and does not poll a hidden document.
- Previous/next controls span the full vertical reading edges. The actual PDF viewport scrolls independently of these stationary controls. Vertical touch movement still pans the document; a tap turns a page. No page dragging was restored.
- Section flags have themed paper, a folded edge and a binding shadow. Hover or keyboard focus extends their width to reveal their title and first-material glimpse, with the existing attached preview. Flags retain their vertical positions; RTL mechanics mirror correctly.

## Curriculum shelf

Outside Study focus, the course toolbar becomes a shallow shelf with tucked themed books and small labelled utility controls. It uses the current batch term containing the course or its clinical-year membership, falling back to the same year and track when curriculum records are unavailable. Real curriculum membership may include a shared course from another study year.

Only the lower part of each book is visible initially. Hover/focus slides out roughly half its cover. The visible strip has a larger transparent hit area for touch and a small course-name label on devices without hover. Clicking opens the existing public/personal course route with the established course-opening transition and restores that course's selected file, PDF page and reading position. The whole shelf is absent in Study focus; no campus header or reveal button is added there.

Phone controls use two compact rows at the shelf edge; the duplicate Tools header button is omitted because the labelled tool strip stays available. The small campus hint sits at the screen edge rather than covering the tools.

## PDF import

The temporary personal PDF testing picker is removed from the course interface. To attach actual course material:

1. Sign in using an account with `content.review`, `content.publish` or `builder.manage`.
2. Select the target material section and choose/drop PDFs on its importer, or open **PDF** in the tool strip. Overview, recordings and external-link sections send imports to Notes.
3. The importer reacts to a file entering the drop zone. After release it shows each filename and size, validation/storage status, real completed-file counts and a success check. The drawer's **Read PDF** action opens the imported document after the visible receipt.

Both the importer and local repository validate the PDF signature, type, nonempty content, 30 MB per-file limit and eight-file batch limit. Overlapping submissions are blocked. Progress counts completed writes; it does not simulate a network upload. IndexedDB success is reported after transaction completion. When device storage is unavailable, the memory fallback is labelled **session only**.

Guests see sign-in guidance, and signed-in accounts without the required capabilities see an access explanation. Import and removal callbacks also guard the current capability result. These preview permissions do not replace server enforcement. PDFs remain device-local and are not published to other students; shared storage still requires the course API.

The earlier temporary-file helper remains unused in the source tree for release continuity. It is not imported by the course route or exposed as a product tool. No test PDFs are included in this source package.

## Hero artwork and motion

The generated tab artwork stays part of each hero background. Copy-area blur is reduced from 9 px to 3 px, with lighter, localised tinting so more of the image remains visible. Copy uses the existing foreground ink token for readability; recruitment fact contrast and the theme palette are retained.

The established Save-to-Library motion, PDF landing/check animation, realistic page surfaces and course entrance remain connected. New shelf, grip and receipt motion have reduced-motion alternatives. No decorative loop or extra animation library was added.

## Verification

Automated regression, strict TypeScript and production build results are recorded for this release in the delivery message. Chromium checks cover normal/focus PDF sizing, full-height edge turns after scroll, movable tools, live timer, role-aware real import, reload persistence, curriculum switching, phone layouts, Arabic RTL, dark/light heroes, reduced motion and native touch panning.

This is responsive Chromium verification, not certification on physical phones or Safari. The inherited large shared-entry chunk advisory remains; PDF engine, campus renderer and course pages stay separately loaded.

# MedClub V0.13.2 — Interaction fidelity and PDF materials

V0.13.2 replaces generic motion with meaningful state changes and rebuilds the course experience around real file-based study materials. Every V0.1–V0.13.1 route, workflow, permission and data boundary remains available.

## Semantic navigation motion

- Navigation icons now contain an initial and destination SVG shape rather than relying on rotation or shaking.
- Bookmark, bell, calendar, search, medical, profile, store and Admin controls receive purpose-specific state changes.
- The shared morph registry matches icons by name so source icons remain owned by their route and the application shell does not import a second copy of every icon.
- Hover, focus-visible and active states share the same visual grammar; reduced motion switches immediately between states.

## Physical discovery surfaces

- Course catalogue entries are closed three-dimensional academic volumes with a spine, page block, inset cover, ribbon and a cover palette derived from each course theme.
- Hover opens the cover only enough to reveal the first-page preview while keeping the complete card as one accessible link.
- Event and opportunity cards now lift as file folders, move a colored divider, reveal secondary information from a sheet behind the face and strengthen the primary action.
- Coarse-pointer and narrow layouts keep all revealed information visible without depending on hover.

## Real notebook behavior

- Course section changes preserve the outer-page position instead of forcing the page back to the notebook top.
- Both the course header and notebook provide a clear route back to the course catalogue.
- Page turns now include front and back sheet surfaces, a moving edge and a travelling shadow so the direction reads as a page turn rather than a generic fade.
- Existing selected resources, bookmarks, reading position, split view and focus mode remain intact.

## PDF material importing

- Slides, notes, questions and the other file-based sections accept one or more real PDF files through a styled picker or drag-and-drop surface.
- The drop surface gives an explicit drag-ready state and animates a PDF sheet landing into a miniature notebook.
- Files are validated as PDFs, limited to 30 MB each and eight files per import, and stored as Blobs in IndexedDB with a safe in-memory fallback.
- Imported files become normal PDF resources, open inside the existing notebook viewer and can be removed from the active section.
- The importer is shown only to authenticated accounts with review, publishing or builder capability.

## Production boundary

This source-only release stores imported PDFs on the current device. Shared materials, moderation, revision history, permanent URLs and multi-device access require authenticated backend storage plus server-side permission and scientific-review enforcement. The UI and repository boundary are ready for that replacement; no device-local upload is presented as a published club resource.

## Performance and accessibility

- No 3D library, WebGL scene, Blender model or new runtime dependency is introduced; the physical effects use semantic HTML and GPU-friendly CSS transforms.
- Route-level lazy loading remains intact.
- Fine-pointer hover enhancements have touch fallbacks.
- RTL reverses opening direction and page movement.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`, forced colors and keyboard focus retain complete functionality.

## Verification

- 206 automated checks cover V0.1–V0.13.2 behavior.
- Strict TypeScript validation and the production Vite build are release gates.
- Real-browser visual acceptance remains required after integrating the source into its host project.

# MedClub V0.13.23 — Reading frame and palettes

Replace the entire existing `src/` directory with this complete tree. Existing project dependencies and configuration remain unchanged. The archive retains all V0.1–V0.13.22 source files, including the PDF importer, study-position storage, persistent bookshelf, notes, GPA tool and permission model.

## Reading space

- Courses lock only the outer document scrollbar. The PDF viewport retains wheel, touch and keyboard scrolling; its scrollbar is visually hidden. Leaving a course releases the document lock.
- Focus mode uses the book frame at the viewport boundary, with 3 px inner framing and no reserved toolbar footer. Section flags overlay the edge instead of resizing the reader. Hover, focus and touch reveal them. Horizontal flags retain separate space for PDF controls, and phone targets remain 44 px.
- The shelf/header is 60 px on desktop and 56 px on phones, reduced from 76 px. Its SVG shoulders now contain the utility buttons at those heights. Below 1201 px, controls use the existing compact panel.
- Shelf book edges are more visible, while the same mounted shelf and its scroll position survive course switching.

## PDF colors

The site appearance automatically controls PDF paper. Entering dark mode remaps neutral white paper to the selected dark surface and neutral black ink to a light reading color. The existing PDF tools include **Page colors**, which independently restores **Original colors** or uses dark paper. Changing site mode or palette resumes automatic paper colors.

This operates on the displayed canvas only. PDF bytes, downloaded files and cached original page rasters remain unchanged. Strongly colored pixels are preserved; neutral pixels inside grayscale photos and diagrams also remap. Choose **Original colors** when inspecting image detail. This is a display preference, not a fidelity-preserving medical-image viewer.

Recoloring runs only when a page is rendered or its palette changes, using a bounded color lookup cache. Existing raster limits remain 1.2 million pixels per page on phones and 2 million on larger screens. No new rendering or animation dependency was added.

## Tools and files

- A deliberate move within 5 px of any viewport edge docks the tools at that edge. The recovery tab is attached to the physical edge. Tap, hover, keyboard reveal, dragging, timer status and saved positions remain available.
- Delete remains permission-aware and only applies to removable local PDFs. A small PDF badge fills its quiet slot; Delete replaces that badge on hover/focus, without shifting the other actions. Touch users receive a visible delete target.
- Import progress, completion reset, review/favorite controls on closed file cards, and deletion failure recovery remain intact.

## Appearance

Open **Appearance** in normal navigation, or **Reading palettes** in the course controls. Choices are:

| Palette | Intended character | Initial mode when selected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MedClub | Original wine and warm paper | Keeps current mode |
| Paper | Warm ivory and restrained ink | Light |
| Dusk | Quiet slate with wine accents | Dark |
| High contrast | Strong text and clearer boundaries | Keeps current mode |
| Tokyo Night | Muted blue/violet, with a day counterpart | Dark |
| Solarized | Deep teal at night and ivory by day | Dark |

Every palette works with the existing direct light → dark → system cycle. Preferences persist on the device, synchronize across tabs and migrate earlier preferences without losing navigation settings. Native labeled radio controls, Arabic text and system forced-color overrides remain available. High contrast is a palette name, not a claim that the whole application has been certified accessible.

Tokyo Night and Solarized are adapted color inspirations, preserving MedClub's wine action color and readable label contrast. No external theme code or package is incorporated. References: [Tokyo Night](https://github.com/folke/tokyonight.nvim), [Solarized](https://ethanschoonover.com/solarized/).

For ordinary student reading, start with Paper during the day or Dusk/Solarized at night. Tokyo Night offers a more colorful alternative without neon animation.

- 76 DOM/state checks pass: 64 inherited checks and 12 new palette, pixel-mapping and route-lock checks.
- Strict application TypeScript passes. Production build passes; the existing shared chunk advisory remains (approximately 1,024 kB). The course page remains route split, approximately 91 kB.

## Notes

The Notes section has publisher notes, course files and private notes attached to the current course. Production must enforce permissions and persist publisher text in the content service/API. Private notes remain isolated by the signed-in account on the device.

The notes tool opens to saved cards. The + icon opens a title/body editor with General or Course association. Existing edits autosave after 600 ms; new notes require Save (or leaving a non-empty draft). Save returns to the list and produces a finite receipt. Edit appears on hover/focus and stays accessible on phones. Delete is available from the editor with confirmation. A left swipe reveals Delete; a deliberate full swipe deletes, while vertical gestures remain scrolling. Deletion offers 10 seconds of Undo. Failed deletion restores the card; failed saves preserve the draft for retry/download. At the 500-note limit a new save is rejected rather than discarding an older note. Lists reveal 20 items at a time with search and Show more.

Focus and Relaxation timers share Start/Pause/Reset controls. Session duration is 1–180 minutes; rest is 0–60 minutes. Finishing a session prepares a **paused** rest period, which the student starts when ready. Finishing rest returns to the configured session. No rest period begins unseen.

Earlier stored preferences and cross-tab synchronization remain compatible; the unused legacy mode component remains solely for migration compatibility.

A theme hover or keyboard focus reveals four lightweight SVG views: Home, Courses, Study reader and Workspace. These are **illustrative layouts using the actual palette tokens**, not screenshots of the live website. Auto playback advances every 2 seconds; selecting a view or theme pauses it. Closing and reopening resets automatic playback. Reduced motion makes it static; hidden browser tabs pause it. On phones, tap a theme and use the view buttons. No generated raster images or animation package is needed.

PDF paper follows both light and dark palettes. Page colors still allows Original colors, and a site appearance change returns the PDF to automatic theme paper. Recoloring affects displayed neutral pixels only, not PDF bytes or cached source rasters; Original colors remains useful when inspecting image detail. Raster memory limits and route-split PDF rendering are retained.

The filename/external/close row is thinner outside focus (32 px for fine-pointer desktop, 44 px touch targets). Focus PDFs always have Close in their own PDF control row; missing URLs and non-PDF readers retain a fallback close control. PDF page buttons, page edges and keyboard turns stop at the file boundaries. They never change course sections. Section turns return after leaving the PDF.

# MedClub V0.13.25 — Study desk and action feedback

V0.13.24 is the exact baseline; earlier release notes remain historical. ## PDF zoom and page movement

The PDF spread sits in a canvas with a physical left-to-right scroll origin, while the pages retain the chosen language direction. Enlarged pages can be panned horizontally with touch, a trackpad, a scrollbar gesture, or the labelled Pan slider. The slider supports keyboard input, appears only when the spread exceeds the reader width, and reserves bottom padding so it does not cover the last line. Panning clamps when the viewport shrinks or zoom changes. PDF page navigation still stops at the first/last page and never changes course sections.

Page movement now uses a narrow paper ribbon: the outgoing face peels away and reveals actual incoming content beneath it. A small highlight and three paper flecks travel along the fold. The effect stays inside the spread, mirrors in RTL and has no rotating text or full-screen curling sheet. Click section transitions use the same paper-peel language. Reduced motion removes the decorative layers. The existing page cache, preview rendering and selection layer remain intact.

## Study tools

The public Study Tools page opens with the timer in its hero. Timer, Notes and GPA selectors below replace the tool in that same space. Opened tools stay mounted so switching tools preserves drafts and timer state. Signed-out users can use the timer; private Notes and saved GPA access retain their account checks.

Public and course timers use the same controls and state helpers: Focus, Relaxation, editable session/rest durations, Start/Pause and Reset. A finished session prepares a **paused** rest period; no rest starts unseen. The public timer persists by account on the device, checks elapsed wall time after backgrounding, and pauses its one-second UI interval while the document is hidden. Course timer completion/docked-handle behavior is unchanged.

The timer has a round alarm-clock face, two bells, feet, twelve ticks and a measured hand/ring. Notes have a notebook binding and layered paper edge. These are CSS/SVG surfaces around real accessible controls, with no new 3D renderer or continuous decorative animation. Course tools inherit the current book cover and paper colors. Both the movable grip and edge recovery handle now match the cover; forced colors retain system colors.

## Undo and deletion feedback

Deleting a PDF or private note sends a labelled paper card along a short arc into a visible bin. Cart items, calendar entries, library collections, private contribution drafts, assessment records and builder blocks use that same finite flight. The source stays in place until the flight finishes; data changes are reported only after the mutation succeeds. Repeated PDF/cart deletion is guarded. Reduced motion and unavailable animation APIs proceed immediately with static receipts.

Undo is available on desktop and phones:

| Editable record | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| Local PDF | Same ID, actual Blob, filename and metadata; fresh viewer URL |
| Private note | Deleted note or the original title/body/course association before an edit |
| Publisher notes | Previous English/Arabic prose |
| Library | Deleted collection, renamed collection, collection membership, removed saved item with its timestamp |
| Calendar | Deleted/edited study entry, including its notes |
| Cart | Removed line or previous quantity |
| Profile | Original editable fields, including both localized strings in the local adapter |
| Private contribution | Deleted/edited draft with its original ID and history |
| Recruitment | Previous editable application draft |
| GPA calculator | Twenty-step account-scoped Undo/Redo for input edits and course-row deletion |
| Academic insights | Deleted assessment attempt or previous/absent confidence rating |
| Page builder | Existing Undo/Redo history; block deletion gains the flight |

GPA Undo/Redo keeps twenty steps while the calculator is open; builder history retains its existing behavior. Global receipts offer 15 seconds of Undo; private note deletion keeps its existing 10-second recovery and note edits offer 15 seconds. Editing notes groups changes from opening the editor through its autosaves into one original before-image. Most reversals compare the affected record to its post-action value, preserving unrelated work and rejecting newer edits. Account changes prevent cross-account Undo, and PDF changes recheck current content-edit permission. A failed recovery keeps a retry action while it remains available. Expired global receipts are dismissed and release their before-image. Governance approvals, publishing, submission, reservations and other committed workflows retain their established rules.

PDFs remain device-local. Blocked storage keeps an explicitly session-only copy. Removing a durable PDF waits for IndexedDB success; an abort preserves the card and file. Undo restores the actual Blob, with the same storage fallback. Shared storage, server authorization and record-version checks are production responsibilities. Optional adapter methods `auth.restoreProfile`, `contributions.restoreDraft`, `insights.restoreAssessment` and `insights.restoreConfidence` are implemented by the local preview; API adapters should implement equivalent authenticated/version-checked operations. Legacy profile adapters can restore the previously displayed input values.

## Covers and appearance

Three new generated textures supplement the existing two: crosshatched Saffiano, brushed suede and diamond embossing. Stable course-ID selection keeps the material consistent on its catalogue cover, shelf book and notebook. Neutral texture layers preserve the course's established cover colors and never overlay PDF content. The new WebP textures are 512 × 512 and add 152,604 bytes in total; the original leather assets remain unchanged.

Appearance retains six Light themes, six Dark themes and System, now in a compact multi-column preset grid. Every preset has a three-color swatch. Playback advances every two seconds, pauses on manual selection, resets after closing/reopening, pauses in hidden tabs and stays static under reduced motion. These are palette/layout previews, not screenshots of the live site.

## What changed

- Reserved a 44 px logical page-turn hit strip beside vertical section flags. The unfocused file reader reserves 64 px for its inset. Expanded flags and previews remain outside that strip, mirrored in Arabic. Previous and next controls have 44 px targets; the PDF canvas and focus frame are preserved.
- Raised leather-grain visibility from 18% to 72%; the shelf uses 78%. The texture fills each cover, with restrained relief around its edges. Cover titles, course code, metadata and actions remain real readable HTML above the material layer.
- Added three generated textures: woven leather, ostrich-style grain and sculpted fluted leather. Eight materials now share a deterministic assignment across catalogue, shelf and opened book; all eight are used by actual sample courses.
- Reduced personal sidebar destinations from 16 to 12. **My activities** groups Events, Opportunities and Contributions; their existing routes and workflows remain intact. Its local icons are distinct and static. Four core mobile destinations are unchanged, with My activities in More.
- Profile opens from the personal header icon and sidebar avatar. Settings remains a sidebar destination. Notifications remain in the personal header and now also appear in the public header for authenticated accounts.
- Both notification shortcuts use the same unread state and shared request. Notification queries are scoped to the current account. Signed-out public visitors do not mount the notification shortcut or request notification data. The badge is capped visually at 99+, while its accessible label gives the full count.

## Source and integration boundaries

All 717 V0.13.25 files are retained. Profile, notifications, events, opportunities, contributions, recruitment, mentorship and existing course routes are preserved. The new `/my/activities` entry opens `/my/events`; the three local tabs retain their established URLs. It remains protected by the existing authentication route.

No runtime dependency was added. Texture assets use optimized 512 × 512 WebP; existing course colors and appearance themes remain in control of the covers.

This is a complete source deliverable, not a production deployment. The existing device-local preview services remain in use. The new notification shortcut does not add server push or a new messaging backend.

## Proposed next features

These are proposals, not features implemented in this release. They extend the existing notes, timer, course, calendar, activity and governance systems. Connected Learning Materials remains excluded.

| Feature | Concrete student value | Main work required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PDF margin notes | Attach a private note or highlight to a specific passage; open directly at that page later. | PDF text/rectangle anchors, source-version handling, private note storage and cross-device sync. |
| Recall desk | Turn student-authored highlights into question cards, schedule short spaced reviews, and retain source-page references. | Review scheduling, answer feedback, accessible question formats; no unreviewed generated medical answer presented as fact. |
| Exam sprint planner | Work backwards from real exam dates and available hours; reorganize study blocks after missed sessions. | Student-supplied deadlines, editable workload assumptions, calendar integration and conflict checks. |
| Case journeys | Work through tutor-reviewed cases as clues appear, explain reasoning, then compare with an authored explanation. | Reviewed case authoring and versioning, teaching rubrics and assessment history. |
| Offline course packs | Download selected PDFs and notes with visible size and freshness; continue studying without a connection. | Service worker/cache strategy, storage limits, per-account access, file revisions and reconnection conflict handling. |
| Verified campus portfolio | Collect confirmed event attendance, publications and contributions into a selectively shareable portfolio. | Verifier permissions, evidence records, revocation, privacy controls and export. |
| Quiet study rooms | An invited group shares a timer and goals; personal notes remain private. | Durable rooms, presence, consent, low-bandwidth updates and abuse controls. |
| Living campus progress | A private campus or notebook gains small visible improvements after recorded study milestones and verified contributions. | Real evidence-backed milestones and a calm-mode alternative; no public exposure of private study activity. |

My recommended first pair is PDF margin notes plus the recall desk: it connects the present study environment to actions students can return to.

Research grounding for the learning strategy: Trumble et al., systematic review of distributed and retrieval practice in health professions education, DOI `10.1007/s10459-023-10274-3`. Heterogeneous studies support the strategy; they do not certify the outcome of a proposed MedClub feature. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37615780/

Offline architecture reference: MDN, Offline and background operation. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Guides/Offline_and_background_operation

# MedClub V0.13.27 — Study Hub

This release adds PDF margin notes, recall practice, offline course packs, an evidence-backed campus portfolio, and quiet study rooms. Every V0.13.26 source file is retained. The previous study environment, theme system, PDF controls, role separation, personal navigation and activity routes remain included. No Connected Learning Materials system was introduced.

## How to try it

Sign in, then open **Your study desk** from the personal dashboard or the existing Focus page. The sidebar still has 12 destinations.

- **Margin notes:** open a real course PDF → PDF tools → Margin notes. Add a note on the active page, or choose Place on PDF and tap a point/select text. Notes are private, versioned and anchored to the file revision. Convert one into a recall card from the note panel. Closing the panel restores the full PDF space.
- **Recall:** `/my/study/recall`. Create a course question/answer or use a margin note. The answer stays hidden until revealed; Again/Hard/Good/Easy schedules the next review. View/edit your cards, delete with Undo, and keep self-ratings distinct from exam results.
- **Offline packs:** `/my/study/offline`. Choose a course with real PDF files, or add a personal PDF to the private pack. Download stores actual Blobs in account-scoped IndexedDB; progress/cancel, checksum/expiry checks, complete-pack replacement and remove/Undo are supported. Open the downloaded PDF from the pack. Notes/cards are read-only download snapshots. Cold offline launch requires the supplied build step below.
- **Portfolio:** `/my/portfolio`. Create an evidence-backed achievement, submit it, and let a distinct authorized reviewer verify it. Publications use content-review access; other campus records use event-management access in the preview. Reviewers can revoke verification. Sharing starts off; explicit consent enables a link containing only name and verified achievements. It excludes private notes, pending claims, internal owner/reviewer IDs and evidence URLs. Local attestations are not institutional certificates.
- **Quiet rooms:** `/my/study/rooms`. Create a room or join with an invite, set a goal, and use the host-controlled focus/rest clock. Capacity is enforced; membership is required to read a room. Presence is based on real local accounts, not invented students. The host leaving finishes the room. The local preview only connects accounts inside this browser.

The new delete controls reuse the existing paper-to-bin effect after the service confirms deletion. Notes/cards/claims/packs support Undo where appropriate; reduced-motion handling remains in place.

## API connection

Read `integration/BACKEND-ADDITIONS.md` and the separate handoff first. It compares the features with all 12 pages of the original requirements document and separately lists older additions that may need backend coverage.

`MedClubServices.studyHub` accepts the typed service in `types/study-hub.ts`. `services/study/http-study.service.ts` implements the proposed contract with auth/CSRF callbacks, request/response mapping, encoded IDs, bounded cursor pagination, version headers, idempotent recall attempts, request cancellation and runtime response checks. `integration/connect-study-hub.ts` composes it with your existing backend adapters.

The OpenAPI file documents 33 proposed operations and 35 schemas. These are not confirmed routes from the existing backend. Supply the actual API specification for a mapping review. The adapter also supports private PDF upload so API-backed margin notes can use stable owned file IDs; it never grants course publishing access.

A live content registry without this adapter reports an unavailable Study Hub service instead of silently using the preview store. Older local helpers for general notes, study state, tool state and appearance preferences still require their own backend sync mappings; these are identified in the handoff rather than disguised as connected services.

## Offline hosting setup

After your normal frontend build, run:

```bash
node src/integration/offline-build.mjs dist
```

Serve generated `dist/medclub-sw.js` at the origin root as JavaScript, over HTTPS or localhost. Keep it out of the SPA HTML fallback. It caches only the static app shell/assets, never private API/PDF requests. The backend auth adapter must define the approved offline-session policy. The source-only archive includes the build helper; add the step to the project's CI/package scripts.

## QA scope

DOM/service tests cover private ownership, stale edits, Undo versions, grading deduplication, evidence validation, distinct reviewer access, public projection/revocation, room membership/capacity/timing, cancelled/failed PDF pack downloads, hashes/expiry, HTTP transport/schema failures, and generated service-worker cache boundaries. These are automated checks, not a claim of actual device rendering or animation quality.

Source CSS checks cover inherited responsive/RTL constraints and theme color pairs. New screens use existing theme tokens, compact grouping, 44px controls, normal document scrolling, RTL text and reduced-motion alternatives. No runtime package was added. The existing large shared entry chunk advisory remains.

Live-browser QA is unverified. The applicable [Sites skill](skill://plugin_connector_1p_689987207de08191979cf68eca2941c6/sites/SKILL.md) states: “If `$control-browser` is unavailable, skip browser QA.” That browser-control capability was unavailable here. Check real PDF rendering, mobile overlays/pin placement, cold offline launch and live room timing on staging.

- **Offline course packs**: store permitted course PDF snapshots on this device with their margin/recall snapshots. Successful import/download resets the form without removing the saved pack. Static application assets require the existing offline worker build step.

The UI distinguishes connection failure, shows retry, separates real participants from open seats, reports completion, and confirms host departure. Successful create/join resets the draft. The lobby tucks away inside a selected room.
