# MedClub V0.13.3 — Reading space and navigation restraint

V0.13.3 refines the V0.13.2 interaction system around two principles: study files need a generous reading surface, and motion should explain a destination rather than decorate every control. Every V0.1–V0.13.2 route, workflow, permission and data boundary remains available.

## Larger PDF reading surface

- PDF documents use a tall responsive viewport instead of the previous short embedded window.
- The primary PDF reader avoids a second constrained scrolling region, leaving document scrolling to the native PDF viewer.
- Single-pane, split-view and mobile modes receive separate height limits so the document remains useful without breaking the notebook layout.
- The existing page bookmark, open-file fallback, save state, review state and reading-position behavior remain intact.

## Restrained, semantic icon motion

- Morphing is limited to actual navigation destinations and filter tabs.
- Expand, collapse, hide, pin, search, language, appearance and header utility icons remain visually stable.
- Each mapped destination icon has its own active form; unrelated tabs no longer converge on the same generic checkmark or repeated symbol.
- Reduced-motion mode changes icon state without animation.

## Fixed navigation controls

- The main desktop navigation remains fixed to the viewport.
- Pin and hide controls now live inside the navigation panel instead of occupying a separate outer rail.
- On fine pointers, the controls appear when the navigation is hovered or keyboard focus enters it.
- Touch and coarse-pointer layouts keep the controls visible because hover is unavailable.
- The hidden-navigation edge handle remains available for restoring the navigation.

## Responsive and performance boundaries

- The update uses the existing Lucide icons, semantic HTML and CSS transforms; no runtime animation or 3D dependency is added.
- Route-level lazy loading remains unchanged.
- RTL, keyboard focus, forced colors, touch input and reduced motion remain supported.
- The PDF viewer uses native browser rendering, so its toolbar and exact pagination behavior remain browser-dependent.

## Verification

- 213 automated checks cover V0.1–V0.13.3 behavior.
- Strict TypeScript validation and the production Vite build are release gates.
- Real-browser visual acceptance remains required after integrating the source into its host project.

# MedClub V0.13.35 — requested performance and control fixes

This complete source release builds on the accepted V0.13.34. Back up the host

## Route responsiveness

Navigation commits the destination immediately instead of waiting for a fixed
140 ms exit timer. Lazy modules and query-driven pages keep their loading UI visible
and interactive. Ready content receives a brief, restrained arrival fade. Scroll
restoration, fragment links, keyboard focus and the existing same-desk course switch
remain supported. Height comes from ResizeObserver rather than a synchronous
`offsetHeight` read during navigation. Selection geometry is measured in a queued
frame with persistent observers, avoiding observer teardown and class changes on
every route. Reduced motion still bypasses motion.

## PDF controls and rendering

- Animation progress updates the visual turn leaf independently. The reader tree
  updates at the turn's start, midpoint and finish instead of every animation frame.
  The existing ribbon turn and previous/next keyboard behavior remain.
- The spread and its animated copies share a cached paper-color display raster.
  Paper conversion works in small pixel strips and yields between strips, allowing
  other UI tasks to run. The source raster, colored figures and PDF bytes are intact.
  Original colors is still available. Changing paper tone no longer rebuilds the
  selectable text layer. Search and page-note anchors retain their existing data.
- A single raster job runs at a time. Visible requests precede queued prefetches;
  a visible request promotes an existing prefetch. Evicted queued pages are canceled
  instead of rendering obsolete zoom sizes. Closing rejects queued work, cancels the
  active render and releases cached canvases. Eight source pages remain the cache
  limit, with at most one current paper-color copy for each cached source raster.
- ResizeObserver supplies reader dimensions without immediate post-render width
  reads. Shared study-tool values/callbacks and note arrays stay stable when their
  contents do not change.
- Side turn targets are 44px wide and 120–280px tall, bounded by their reading
  surface. The close control retains its separate 44px toolbar cell. Tooltips remain.
- Section-turn visual snapshots skip the redundant PDF text-selection DOM and cap
  their copied DOM/pixels. These limits apply only to temporary animation faces.

Pin/hide controls remain absolutely positioned over the status row, with no change

# MedClub V0.13.36 — PDF loading, controls and page turns

This complete `src` release builds on V0.13.35. Back up the host project's `src`,
then replace it with the enclosed directory. Retain the host configuration and
dependencies. No package dependency is added. No deployment is included.

## Loading and document lifetime

The PDF engine imports its 198 bundled CMap/font/WASM asset URLs lazily. It loads
an asset when PDF.js requests it instead of eagerly importing all asset modules
when the reader opens. The bundled support assets remain in the source.
Canceled reader effects are checked before creating a loading task, including
React development StrictMode's initial setup/cleanup replay.

The document-opening effect depends on the file URL and an explicit retry. Page
turns, zoom, searching, bookmarking, notes and paper colors do not reopen the file.
Closing or changing files still destroys the loading task, cancels rendering and
releases owned caches and worker resources.

## Stable page display

Raster identity is independent of zoom. Pages are prepared for the reader's maximum
zoom and scaled for display, including the transparent text-selection stage. Zoom
no longer clears/rebuilds canvas pixels or reconstructs text spans. A real width or
spread-layout change can still require a different raster.

The renderer exposes a synchronous lookup for ready display pixels. Cached pages
are painted before the frame is displayed, avoiding a loading flash when returning
to a prepared page. The next spread's complete display rasters are prepared before
the existing ribbon animation starts. The current spread stays visible while a
cold destination is being prepared, and stale preparations cannot commit after
the file, page, layout or appearance changes. Nearby-page prefetch includes paper
colors rather than only the original white source raster.

The ribbon's position moves with a transform instead of an animated `left`
property. The active PDF turn allocates its visual layers only for its lifetime.
The existing page-turn appearance, direction, keyboard controls and reduced-motion
behavior remain.

## Text and color preparation

Visible raster completion no longer waits for text extraction. Text data and
selection DOM have their own caches. TextLayer receives a ReadableStream in batches
of at most 80 items, yielding a UI task between batches. This uses the streaming
interface already implemented by the bundled, unmodified PDF.js 6.4.299; its narrow
TypeScript declaration now describes that interface. Dense pages do not create all
selection spans in one synchronous task. Cached selection DOM is reused when a
page returns. Search uses cached text and yields during a multi-page scan.

Where Worker, OffscreenCanvas and ImageBitmap are available, a reader-owned worker
converts neutral paper/ink pixels off the UI thread. The main thread transfers the
result to a display canvas. Source PDF bytes, original rasters and strongly colored
figure pixels remain intact. A blocked/unsupported worker falls back to the existing
cooperative pixel-strip conversion. Worker errors, cancellation, pending requests,
late responses and bitmap transfers have explicit cleanup. Original colors remains
available. Changing paper colors does not rebuild the text layer.

The existing limits remain: eight source rasters, at most one current toned display
copy per source, and one active raster job. Ready-display lookups are bounded to
16 entries. Text data is bounded to 16 pages; selection DOM is released with its
source page. The larger page-turn targets and separate close-button cell are kept.

## Preserved features

All V0.13.35 files remain present. Changes are limited to the PDF performance path,
its types and release documentation. Themes, dashboard colors, navigation controls,
language ordering, bell animation, liquid-glass appearance, course notes/anchors,
private-note storage, bookmarking and the profile-library save flight are retained.

## Verification and limits

React DOM interaction checks exercise the real PdfBook/usePageTurn components with
a mocked DOM and PDF engine in single-page, two-page and Arabic RTL configurations.
They verify one document open per file, no raster rebuild or canvas repaint for
zoom/search/bookmark controls, correct page-turn commits, appearance-only updates,
file replacement and close cleanup. The same harness on V0.13.35 reproduces two
initial opens in development StrictMode and new raster requests/canvas repaint on
zoom; the updated reader removes those operations in the harness.

Executable checks also cover pixel parity, the actual worker message handler,
transfer failure, worker fallback/disposal, dense text order/positions, streamed
text cancellation, selection-cache reuse, raster readiness independent of text,
ready-display invalidation and stable raster geometry across all zoom values.
Previous private-note/version/undo and preserved-motion checks remain passing.
Changed TS/TSX entries pass syntax checks; isolated rendering/worker/text/geometry
and turn helpers pass strict TypeScript checks.

The upload is source-only and lacks the host package manifest, dependency lockfile
and build configuration. A full production build or live-browser performance trace
could not be run here. These checks establish the changed lifecycle/rendering
behavior; they do not establish real-browser frame times or guarantee that every
performance warning disappears. File/network speed and PDF complexity still affect
cold loading. Similarweb extension CORS/connection errors are outside this reader.

# MedClub V0.13.43 — stable building restoration and arrival stars

This complete source folder builds on V0.13.42 and changes the registration campus restoration only. No dependency was added. Replace your project's existing `src` folder and retain its configuration and dependencies.

## Why details were changing

V0.13.42 changed the entire scene to another independently generated image after each milestone. Those images redrew small details in buildings that had already been repaired. The intermediate images remain in the source archive, but registration no longer switches between them.

The updated renderer keeps the awaiting photograph and one fixed restored photograph mounted. Each completed field reveals its building's region from that same restored photograph. Previously completed buildings keep their original restored pixels through all later milestones. Soft alpha edges blend the regions; the photographs themselves are not blurred, transformed by the animation, or crossfaded. Completing the last field exposes the whole restored scene, including the remaining ground.

## Arrival effect

The renderer waits for the path's actual stroke transition to finish, including when reaching Create Account changes the path speed. It then restores the building and emits a finite burst at the exact path endpoint:

- Eighteen stars expand radially, with alternating sizes and short comet tails.
- A central star flashes briefly with two expanding light rings.
- Highlights combine warm light with the current theme's path color.
- Each burst finishes independently, so continuing to type does not truncate it. At most three bursts coexist; finished SVG nodes and timers are removed.

The existing shared path animation and home/sign-in effects are retained. The new starburst belongs to registration restoration. English/Arabic use the same scene coordinates and mirrored artwork. Phone artwork has its own aligned endpoint and reveal-region map.

Invalidating a field removes its restored region and hides any corresponding arrival burst. Out-of-order completion remains supported. Reduced motion keeps restoration functional and suppresses the fireworks. Hidden pages clear active bursts. Source photographs remain sharp and fixed.

## Verification

- Strict TypeScript and production Vite build.
- Registration flows on desktop and phone, in light/dark modes and English/Arabic.
- Screenshot comparisons of previously restored building details after each later milestone, including the fully restored final image.
- Actual path-endpoint alignment, completed path stroke before arrival, eighteen finite animated stars, and cleanup after each burst.
- Invalid fields, Back/Edit, verification, out-of-order completion and reduced-motion behavior.

The PDF reader and all other source files outside the restoration change and version documentation retain their V0.13.42 contents. Browser checks use Chromium automation; device-specific rendering and performance still depend on the user's browser and hardware.

| --- | --- | --- |

| Mentorship | Accepted mentorship requests | 1, 3, 6 |
| Contribution | Approved or published contributions | 1, 3, 6 |

Completing 6, 18 or 36 distinct resource/card reviews can also develop the community, mentorship and contribution buildings, so social participation is optional. Repeat reviews of the same card do not multiply that count. Visits and timer minutes do not count. Earned stages persist when records are removed or the student takes a break. These are motivational visual milestones, not academic proficiency measurements.

The buildings link to their personal destinations, with ordinary text links as a touch and image-failure fallback. Short path and light sequences use the existing visible-minute scheduler, stop while the page is hidden or outside the viewport, and respect reduced motion. The campus stays quiet when the exam hero is active.

| `/learn/electronic-exams`                        | Public course catalogue and exam entry         |
| `/my/exams`                                      | Personal course catalogue and resume action    |
| `…/set/:examId`                                  | Practice/self-test setup                       |
| `…/set/:examId/review`                           | Review a question set                          |
| `…/set/:examId/print`                            | Print a question set                           |
| `…/attempt/:attemptId`                           | Active question session                        |
| `…/attempt/:attemptId/results`                   | Finished session review                        |
| `…/history`, `…/notebook`, `…/wrong`, `…/search` | Attempts, saved questions, mistakes and search |
| `/admin/exams`                                   | Exam content administration                    |

The `…` routes exist beneath both student entry paths. The personal path requires MedClub authentication; the preview public path can also demonstrate the flow as a guest.

## API boundary

No original Next.js API routes, Supabase clients, SQL, API credentials or backend requests were copied. The UI depends on `ExamService` in `types/exams.ts`. A future adapter is injected as `services.exams`; [integration/EXAMS-FRONTEND.md](./integration/EXAMS-FRONTEND.md) documents the contract.

In MedClub's sample configuration, the adapter is a clearly labeled, device-local preview. Its starter questions demonstrate interface actions; they are not a medical question bank. Preview attempts do not grant campus growth or academic-readiness credit. Data stays in the current browser; it does not synchronize across devices. A live MedClub configuration without an exam adapter shows an unavailable state rather than silently displaying preview questions.

The preview separates guest/account attempts, bookmarks and custom sets. Storage denial falls back to the current session with a visible notice. Corrupt stored data reports an error rather than resetting it silently. The session maintains a private recovery draft and serial save queue; version conflicts and save failures offer retry or reload. No future server endpoint or authentication scheme was guessed.

## Performance and verification

- Strict TypeScript checking and the production build passed. Exam UI pages are lazy loaded; no PDF engine is opened by the exam flow.
- 56 hub/session layout checks passed: English/Arabic, light/dark and widths from 320 to 2560 pixels. Checked controls maintained at least 44px height without horizontal page overflow.
- 36 theme checks passed: all nine palettes, both modes and both languages. Sample answer text and primary-button contrast exceeded 4.5:1.
- Student flow checks covered save/resume/reload, exact question restoration, flags/bookmarks, practice and self test, results, mistakes, custom filters, search, printing, keyboard navigation and reduced motion. Admin checks covered creation, editing, image attachment, import validation, publishing, reporting, resolution and confirmed deletion.
- Model checks covered account separation, admin authorization, frozen question snapshots, conflict handling, idempotent finishing, scoring, paged notebooks, unavailable services, storage failure and formatting/import edge cases.
- The timer advanced without any mutations to the question panel. In a controlled mobile Chromium run at fourfold CPU throttling, 12 keyboard page changes took approximately 34–108ms, including automation overhead. These are local observations, not a guarantee for every browser, device or later API.
- The existing My Space scenarios passed. The real eight-page PDF fixture passed 48 balanced-frame checks across both languages, both navigation orientations, six widths and normal/focus modes after layout settling. PDF-reader source and styles were unchanged.

The existing large main application-chunk build warning remains. This release does not connect or test real exam APIs, cross-device persistence or a proctored assessment backend.

The application UI was adapted for MedClub's React/Vite services, navigation, authorization, localization and themes. # V0.2 academic design

## Direction

V0.2 treats academic navigation as a journey, not a conventional card catalogue. The visual idea changes with the task:

| Area              | Visual metaphor        | Interaction                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Learn gateway     | Two connected worlds   | Pointer-following light and layered orbit                      |
| Basic Sciences    | Batch passport         | Progress seal, current-term stamp and lift/reveal hover        |
| Clinical Sciences | Connected path         | Oversized year numerals, changing dark surfaces and pulse line |
| Batch home        | Academic identity card | Current/archive switch and native expandable archive terms     |
| Clinical year     | Year chapter           | Current-focus glass panel and ordered focus strip              |
| Course            | Course atlas           | Section rail, central material stage and compact context card  |

Course accents are configuration-driven: red, russet, olive and purple records set the course atlas highlight, soft background light and active section. This preserves a coherent MedClub system while letting courses feel distinct.

## Motion rules

- Page entry: 320 ms fade/settle with a 550 ms line trace.
- Cards: short lift and small directional-arrow movement.
- Portal light: follows pointer position without moving content.
- Decorative course orbit: slow 24-second rotation.
- No scroll hijacking, delayed content, cursor replacement or full-page WebGL.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` removes orbit/pulse animation and hover transforms. Framer Motion entry transitions also resolve immediately.

## Responsive behavior

At wide widths, the course atlas uses a section rail, content stage and context card. Below 1200 px the context card becomes a horizontal row. Below 960 px the section rail becomes horizontally scrollable and all journey card grids become single-column. Below 768 px, academic navigation remains touch-friendly above the existing bottom dock and dense metadata stacks vertically.

The interface supports English and Arabic. Directional motion and arrows mirror in RTL; the desktop sidebar remains on the left by the user's design decision.

## Honest preview behavior

Material cards describe their format and audience. They can be saved and inspected, but no sample file opens because the fixture URLs are intentionally null. Batch progress values, course assignments and dates are static examples and must be replaced by approved data.

# V0.4 design language

V0.4 makes discovery feel active without turning routine navigation into a spectacle.

## Motion rules

- The welcome veil is short, pointer-transparent and shown once per browser tab.
- Active icons use a one-shot arrival animation; they do not pulse forever.
- Hover motion is small enough to preserve target stability.
- Cards lift and their internal geometry responds, while text stays readable.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` removes all animation through the shared accessibility layer.

## Visual metaphors

- Events use ticket notches, capacity threads and an orbiting campus constellation.
- Opportunities use a door/portal sculpture, deadline orbits and verified-information cards.
- Red marks action and community energy; russet and warm neutrals carry most surfaces.
- Large organic radii continue the modern V0.2/V0.3 direction instead of returning to rigid rectangles.

## UX boundaries

- Save and register are visually and verbally separate.
- Filters remain native controls with explicit labels.
- Active tabs use `aria-pressed`; navigation uses `aria-current`.
- Mobile filters stack and tab rows scroll horizontally rather than shrinking targets.
- Disabled application actions explain what is missing instead of pretending to work.

# MedClub V0.6 design notes

## Direction

V0.6 extends the medical red/russet system with two related visual metaphors:

- **Mentorship as a guided clinical pathway:** measured pulse lines, connected points and calm directional movement.
- **Scientific review as a safety gate:** staged checkpoints, status rings and clear locked states.

Motion supports meaning. Hovered and active mentorship icons respond like short clinical signals; route reveals remain brief; status changes use restrained emphasis. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes decorative motion without hiding state.

## Information hierarchy

Mentor cards lead with identity, specialty, mentoring areas, capacity and request state. Group-session cards lead with topic, time, format and remaining capacity. The personal workspace separates active plans from discovery so the student can understand what has actually been requested or joined.

Contribution cards always expose current status, last update and next available action. Reviewer feedback appears before revision controls when changes are requested. Approval and publication are visually and functionally distinct.

## Trust boundaries

- Illustrative mentor data is labelled and must be verified before launch.
- Q&A includes an educational-only boundary and should never invite personal health details.
- Rights/reference fields are visible because scientific trust is part of the interaction, not hidden administration.
- Locked under-review and approved states prevent misleading local edits.
- No student-facing publish action exists.

## Responsive and RTL behavior

Desktop retains the collapsible vertical rail and optional horizontal preference. Phones retain horizontal bottom navigation and put secondary destinations in the personal menu. Grids collapse to one column without changing source order. Logical CSS properties and bilingual messages support RTL; scroll cues follow the available direction rather than assuming left-to-right.

## Future API handoff

The screens communicate workflow state but never claim server authority. Real-time capacity, mentor availability, reviewer identity, publication and notifications must come from authenticated services. The current local adapters are explicitly preview infrastructure.

# MedClub V0.7 design notes

## Direction

V0.7 treats the store as a **clinical supply shelf**, not a generic ecommerce template. Deep medical red and russet frame calm warm surfaces. Product cards use rounded asymmetric shapes, layered specimen-like labels and controlled scan-line responses instead of hard rectangular tiles.

The product visuals are intentionally icon-led because verified photography was not supplied. They create a distinctive visual system without presenting invented merchandise images as real products.

## Motion language

- Hover and keyboard focus send a short scanning line through a product card.
- Product objects subtly settle and orbit instead of floating continuously.
- Store-tab icons animate on hover and remain visibly energized while active.
- Page transitions reuse the established clinical pulse/signal language.
- Reservation progress is directional and restrained, emphasizing state rather than decoration.

`prefers-reduced-motion` removes decorative scanning, orbit and transition movement while preserving every label, status and action.

## Information hierarchy

Catalog cards lead with product identity, category, stock and price. Detail pages move variant and quantity choices beside the product context. The cart keeps line-level options editable and places the reservation summary in a clear sticky tray on wide screens.

My Orders belongs to the personal workspace. It leads with status and next action, then shows item snapshots, collection details and totals. Cancellation appears only when the current state allows it.

## Trust boundaries

- Products, prices, stock and collection details are visibly illustrative.
- The CTA says reserve for collection; it never claims a payment was made.
- No card or other payment fields exist.
- Order totals are deterministic snapshots, but browser storage is not financial authority.
- Real product photography and supplier claims must be verified before launch.

## Responsive and RTL behavior

Desktop retains the collapsible vertical rail and optional horizontal preference. Phones retain horizontal navigation. The asymmetric product grid collapses without changing semantic order. Logical CSS properties and bilingual messages support RTL, while buttons and status paths preserve a predictable reading sequence.

## Future API handoff

The screens communicate the intended customer flow but never claim server authority. Real-time inventory, reservations, checkout, fulfillment, refunds, financial reporting and notifications must come from authenticated services. The current local adapter is preview infrastructure only.

# MedClub V0.8 design direction

## Concept: the identity threshold

Authentication is the transition from the public medical community into a student's private study world. The screen uses two related surfaces: a deep red/russet living medical field and a warm, quiet task surface. The form is visible immediately; spectacle never blocks access.

## Signature visual

The decorative WebGL composition suggests cellular motion, a double helix and connected learning without showing literal clinical imagery. Pointer response is restrained and the palette stays within MedClub red, russet, warm white and ink. Layered curves, light bloom and subtle grid texture replace hard rectangular page structure.

## Motion rules

- Motion communicates entry, focus and account-state changes.
- WebGL remains decorative, capped and pausable.
- Auth forms use short directional transitions instead of long introductions.
- Hover and active feedback follows the existing pulse/scan language.
- Reduced-motion users receive stable opacity and static-field treatments.

## Navigation repair language

Scrollbars are hidden without disabling scrolling. Soft directional shadows reveal more destinations and reverse as the user moves through the rail. The cue is quieter than another button and works in both vertical and horizontal orientations.

## UX guardrails

- The primary account task appears in the first viewport.
- Errors are local, specific and recoverable.
- Password visibility is user-controlled.
- Return paths cannot leave the app origin.
- Recovery does not reveal whether an email exists.
- Browser-local preview boundaries are visible; the interface never claims production security.

# MedClub V0.9 design direction

## Concept: the clinical rounds board

Recruitment is treated as a transparent working process rather than a marketing page. The opening screen combines a dark medical signal field with warm, tactile role cards and a visible six-stage path. Students can understand the role, commitment and next stage before giving information.

## Signature behavior

- The hero signal uses quiet rings, nodes and a heartbeat rhythm without literal clinical imagery.
- Position cards have team-specific accents, asymmetric curves and small “signal” details.
- Hover movement is brief and restrained; active navigation icons scan and pulse.
- Application stages connect visually so the current step is never hidden in a status badge alone.
- Onboarding progress and volunteer hours feel operational, not decorative.
- V0.8 authentication remains the only WebGL surface; V0.9 is CSS-only.

## UX rules

- Public role facts remain readable without signing in.
- Signed-out application actions preserve a safe internal return path.
- Draft and submit are separate actions; screening never starts implicitly.
- Closed roles remain readable but cannot accept a draft.
- Student-facing status history is chronological and specific.
- Membership, symbolic titles and permissions are visibly separated.
- All device-local behavior carries an honest preview notice.

## Accessibility and responsive rules

- Form controls have stable IDs and concise accessible names.
- Recruitment navigation and team tabs hide native scrollbars without disabling scroll.
- Touch targets remain large and text inputs use at least 16px text on mobile.
- Six workflow stages reflow to three and then two columns instead of overflowing.
- Logical properties support RTL and directional arrows mirror where necessary.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` removes orbit, pulse and lift animations.
